deed: ארגון איסראייד שולח צוות חילוץ ורפואה לחלץ ולטפל בפצועי רעידת האדמה בהאיטי
title: IsraAID sent 15 volunteers to treat those injured in the Haiti earthquake, and stayed to work there until 2018

trailer.text: IsraAID is an Israel-based non-governmental organization that responds to emergencies around the world, and its founders are Shachar Zahavi and Mully Dor.
In 2010 it served as a coordinating body for 17 Israeli and Jewish humanitarian organizations.
The team, made up entirely of volunteers, arrived on Saturday in Port-au-Prince and immediately began treating the wounded at the site of a collapsed hospital.
It was part of a broad Israeli and Jewish effort, and IsraAID continued to operate in Haiti until 2018.

glance.label: Later
glance.value: A children's education center in the Pétion-Ville camp

stations.title: Messages in the middle of the night

paragraphs.text: According to eJewishPhilanthropy, the people of Haiti were suffering from harsh economic conditions long before January 12, 2010.
Then came the earthquake.
Judy Amit of the JDC noted that Haiti played a critical role in saving Jews during the Holocaust period.
Text messages came in to Shachar Zahavi's phone in the middle of the night.
The question in them was what to do about Haiti.
Zahavi is the chairman of IsraAID.
His coalition also includes funding organizations, among them the American Jewish Committee, B'nai B'rith International and UJA-Federation of Greater Toronto.
On Friday the IsraAID team was trying to find a way into Haiti from the neighboring Dominican Republic.
According to Zahavi, there were two options on the table: a flight from the Dominican Republic, or renting a bus or off-road vehicles and driving across the border.
At the Port-au-Prince airport, planes on the ground lacked the fuel to take off, so there was no room for additional aid flights to land.
According to Zahavi, an American organization called Operation Blessing shipped a container full of medical equipment and aid for the team from Miami to Port-au-Prince.
Other Israeli organizations were also looking for a way to get there.
Israeli aid workers waited in Israel for a route to Haiti to open, and a Magen David Adom representative said on Friday that clearance to leave had not yet been received.
Five Magen David Adom paramedics reached Port-au-Prince only on Monday, overland, after landing in the Dominican Republic.
ZAKA rescuers joined the Mexican delegation, aboard the Mexican Air Force Hercules aircraft.
Daniel Biran is Israel's ambassador for administrative affairs, and unofficially Israel's logistics man for global emergencies.
He arrived in Haiti on January 14 via Santo Domingo.
The IsraAID group, 15 people, arrived on Saturday in Port-au-Prince.
It immediately began treating the wounded at the site of a collapsed hospital near the city center.
All the team members were volunteers.
Alan Schneider, an IsraAID logistics volunteer, had previously been on the organization's missions in Chad, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Kenya and Georgia.
He said he had never seen destruction on such a scale.
Zahavi said that IsraAID members always carry an Israeli flag and hang it wherever they work, and that they do nothing covertly.
According to a message from a team member in the field, Jessica Hartelin, a six-year-old girl, was pulled from the rubble by locals nearly six days after the earthquake.
According to the same message, she was rushed to the clinic and treated by the IsraAID/FIRST medical team.

stations.title: A field hospital in a backyard

paragraphs.text: An IDF team set up a field hospital near a soccer stadium to treat survivors.
The site was the backyard of one of Haiti's few Jewish residents.
According to J., Israel was the first country to set up a field hospital after the earthquake.
Israeli civilians and reserve soldiers built and maintained surgical tents, a pediatrics tent, a radiology tent and a tent for newborn and premature babies.
Biran said that the hospital was ready within eight hours, and that hundreds of patients quickly flooded it.
When the team realized how fragile the situation was, it put up another tent.
According to Biran, the Israeli army eats kosher food even in emergency situations.
The IDF hospital was one of the only places in the city where Haitians could receive advanced medical treatment.
Dr. Richard Besser of ABC said that "They were up and running on Saturday morning, way ahead of the United States hospital."
Biran said: "If we were not there, the people [we were helping] would be dead in the street."
On Saturday Israeli doctors delivered a baby boy at the hospital, and his mother said she would name him Israel.
Dr. Avi Abergel, a gynecologist with the Israeli mission, held a premature baby born in the field hospital.
According to J., the team treated more than 1,110 patients.
According to the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the team performed 319 successful surgeries and delivered 16 babies, three of them by caesarean section.
ZAKA is made up of Orthodox Jewish volunteers.
Before the end of the week, ZAKA rescuers pulled eight students out alive from the wreckage of a collapsed university building.
According to the Jewish Journal, an Israeli team helped rescue two female students buried under the ruins of a university in Port-au-Prince.
The IDF rescue force led or took part in the rescue of four people.
In the end, the Home Front Command decided to stop searching for survivors, because the chance of finding anyone alive was slim.
The head of the ZAKA delegation, Mati Goldstein, wrote that the acrid smell of bodies hangs in the air everywhere.
Biran said that everything had collapsed, that people had nothing and that there was nowhere to bury the bodies.
In February, IsraAID, together with other organizations such as Operation Blessing, opened a child education center in the Pétion-Ville camp, the largest refugee camp in the Port-au-Prince area.
IsraAID's policy is to stay on the ground after the emergency and set up programs that will be handed over to skilled local residents.
According to Zahavi, IsraAID ran a medical facility, an agriculture program, a youth empowerment center and a program for women affected by violence in the camps in Haiti.
According to Zahavi, most of the money for the programs was donated by Jewish federations in North America.
Ben Kachir said that after the earthquake he joined IsraAID and Tevel b’Tzedek in Haiti without knowing anything about the country.
As of January 2015, IsraAID was the only Israeli non-governmental organization still operating in Haiti.
In all, it worked there between 2010 and 2018.
Through MASHAV, Israel established a trauma and emergency room at the Central Hospital in Cap Haitien, and was a partner in setting up a clinic in Léogâne.
The need remained great.
According to the UN, four years after the earthquake about 172,000 people remained displaced in camps, and 600,000 lived in severe food insecurity.
According to Israel21c, five years after the earthquake, of the 1.5 million people initially displaced, about 85,000 were estimated to remain in temporary tent camps.
The international media gave wide coverage to Biran and the Israeli medical and rescue professionals for the efficiency with which they set up a functioning hospital.
According to JTA, the visible presence of the Israeli workers in Haiti helped promote a positive image of Israel, in a world used to seeing it in a negative light.
Biran said that he was sure it was good for the Israeli image, but that the work was not only because of this.
According to Kachir, there was criticism that the work of many organizations that came to Haiti in 2010 was not sustainable.
Zahavi said that he had seen other international organizations bring in ideas and programs that do not work, and that advance study from home did not help in Haiti.
Many international organizations left Haiti, and among the reasons cited were lack of funding and also frustration.
According to eJewishPhilanthropy, the response to Haiti was also an opportunity to improve Israel's public image in the media.

disagreements.question: How long did the field hospital and the rescue team stay?

versions.says: According to J., the Israelis were in Haiti from January 15 to 27
According to the Jewish Journal, the IDF announced on Tuesday that the field hospital and the rescue team would remain for at least another month
According to a message from a team member in the field, Jessica Hartelin was treated by the IsraAID/FIRST medical team, and it was reported that she was saved

According to the Jewish Journal, a Monday night rescue operation came after an unsuccessful rescue mission for a six-year-old girl. The same article also separately reports a six-year-old girl who was rescued from the rubble that same Monday and treated at the IsraAID clinic.

claims.quote: I am sure it is good for the Israeli image, but we’re not doing it only because of this

claims.text: לפי קצ'יר, נטענה ביקורת שעבודת ארגונים רבים שהגיעו ב-2010 לא הייתה בת קיימא.
claims.quote: There has been criticism that the work of many organizations that came here in 2010 was not sustainable

claims.text: זהבי אמר שראה ארגונים בינלאומיים אחרים מביאים רעיונות ותוכניות שלא עובדים, ושלימוד מראש מהבית לא עזר בהאיטי.
claims.quote: We have seen other international organization bring in their own ideas and programs that ultimately don’t work and sometimes have the opposite effect.

claims.text: ארגונים בינלאומיים רבים פרשו מהאיטי, ומהסיבות שצוינו: מחסור במימון וגם תסכול.
claims.quote: Many of the international organizations have pulled out. Reasons cited are lack of funding, but also frustration.

claims.text: לפי eJewishPhilanthropy, התגובה להאיטי הייתה גם הזדמנות לשפר את תדמיתה הציבורית של ישראל בתקשורת.
claims.quote: it can be said to have also been an opportunity to repair the public image of Israel in the media

claims.text: לפי Israel21c, תוך 24 שעות מהרעידה שלח משרד החוץ הישראלי צוות של 220 איש.
claims.quote: Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs sent a 220-person team of rescuers, disaster-management experts and medical personnel.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Journal, צה"ל הודיע ביום שלישי שבית החולים השדה וצוות החילוץ יישארו בהאיטי לפחות עוד חודש.
claims.quote: the IDF announced Tuesday that the Israeli field hospital and rescue crew will remain in Haiti for at least another month.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Journal, מבצע חילוץ ביום שני בלילה בא אחרי משימת חילוץ שלא צלחה עבור ילדה בת שש.
claims.quote: Monday night’s rescue operation came following the unsuccessful rescue mission for a 6-year-old girl

claims.text: בן קצ'יר סיפר שאחרי רעידת האדמה ב-2010 הצטרף לאיסראייד ולתבל בצדק בהאיטי בלי לדעת דבר על המדינה.
claims.quote: Then, after the earthquake in 2010, I joined IsraAID and Tevel b’Tzedek in Haiti without knowing anything about Haiti

claims.text: איסראייד היא ארגון לא ממשלתי מבוסס ישראל שמגיב לחירום ברחבי העולם, ומקימיו הם שחר זהבי ומולי דור.
